h1:
Tawaen Beach, Koh Larn
The Main White-Sand Beach
intro: If it's your first time on Koh Larn and you ask anyone which beach to hit first, most people will say Tawaen Beach. It's the main beach where the big ferries from Bali Hai Pier dock, the busiest spot on the island, and the one place where you get everything in one go: fine white sand, clear water, water sports lined up along the shore, beach chairs to rent and stretch out on, and seafood spots where you can sit for hours. We've pulled together what actually helps, how to get there, rough prices for activities, and the things worth knowing before you go.

blocks.html: Tawaen Beach sits on the east side of Koh Larn, facing the sea and catching a pretty morning sun. It's the beach where the big passenger ferries from Bali Hai Pier in Pattaya dock directly, so most people start their Koh Larn trip here. The beach runs about a kilometre long, with fine white sand, shallow water you can wade into, and full services from one end to the other. The draw is convenience; the trade-off is that it gets very crowded on weekends. If you want a chiller vibe, you can move on to Samae Beach or Nuan Beach later.

blocks.text: Where Is Tawaen Beach, and Why Is It the Main One?

blocks.html: Tawaen Beach is Koh Larn's front door for day-trippers, because the regular big ferries from Bali Hai mainly drop you at the Tawaen Beach pier. The moment the ferry docks, you're met by shops, gear-rental stalls, and rows of water-sports stands. From this one spot you can rent a beach chair to lounge on, grab an inner tube, catch a songthaew to another beach, or find something to eat. That's why it's become the liveliest hub on the island.

items: Big passenger ferry — leaves from Bali Hai Pier in Pattaya, fare around 30 THB per trip, takes roughly 40–45 min, drops you at Tawaen Beach pier (some runs land at Na Ban pier instead, so check the sign before boarding)

Speedboat — much faster, around 15–20 min to Tawaen Beach, roughly 150–200 THB per head to join a shared boat, or a few thousand THB to charter the whole boat depending on size. Good for groups who don't want to wait for the scheduled ferry

Songthaew on the island — from the Tawaen Beach pier there are songthaews shuttling to other beaches like Samae, Nuan and Thian. Fares run from tens of baht to just over a hundred depending on distance. Always ask the price before getting on

blocks.title: On weekends, go early
blocks.html: On Saturdays, Sundays and long weekends it gets packed, the ferry queues get long, and the beach fills up by late morning. Catch one of the first ferries in the morning and you'll snag a well-placed beach chair, skip the water-sports queues, and enjoy the water while it's still clear before the crowd wades in. On the way back, if you leave in the late afternoon along with everyone else, budget extra time for the ferry wait too.

blocks.text: What Water Sports Are at Tawaen Beach, and How Much?

blocks.html: What makes Tawaen busier than the other beaches is the full lineup of water sports running the length of the shore. The prices below are rough ranges from several operators and can shift with the season, weekends, and how well you bargain. Before any activity, ask the price clearly, confirm whether it's per ride or per person, and always check the gear and life jackets first.

items.name: Banana Boat
items.blurb: The crowd favourite that groups of friends and families do the most. You sit in a row on a banana-shaped inflatable while a speedboat drags you around the bay, waiting to see when it'll flip you into the water. It fits 5–6 people at a time, and it's great for anyone who wants a thrill without a fear of heights.

items.name: Parasailing
items.blurb: Strap into a parachute and let a speedboat pull you up into the air, with a high-angle view over Tawaen Beach and the island. It photographs well and hits a nice level of excitement. Big operators like KL Parasailing even offer pickup on the island. A ride lasts only a few minutes but it's worth the rush.
items.meta: up in the air · high-angle view

items.name: Jet Ski
items.blurb: You drive the jet ski yourself for the rental time you pay for. Speed lovers enjoy it, but it's the activity to be most careful about when it comes to damage-fee agreements. Before renting, photograph and video the machine from every angle, and settle the terms clearly to avoid being hit with a damage claim afterwards.
items.meta: self-drive · watch out for damage fees

items.name: Sea Walker (Underwater Walk)
items.blurb: You wear a helmet with air piped down to it and walk along the sandy seabed, looking at fish and coral without needing to swim. It's great for people who want to see the underwater world but are nervous in water. It's usually sold as a package that includes the boat, and it costs more than the surface activities.

items.name: Snorkeling
items.blurb: Rent a mask and snorkel to look at coral and fish in the shallows, or buy a boat tour that takes you out to clearer spots around the island. It won't blow your budget and you get to see real marine life, suitable for all ages, though how clear the water is depends on the weather that day.
items.meta: rent gear yourself or buy a boat tour

items.name: Kayak / Inner Tube
items.blurb: A chill option for people who don't want anything intense. Rent a kayak to paddle along the shore, or grab an inner tube to float in the shallows and soak up the sun. It suits kids and anyone here to relax rather than chase a thrill.
items.meta: chill · good for kids and families
items.price: tube/kayak, tens to just over a hundred THB

blocks.title: Safety first
blocks.html: Before any water sport, check that the life jacket is complete and cinches tight, ask clearly whether the price is per ride or per person, and settle the damage terms before you pay, especially for jet skis, which in some cases come with drama over inflated damage claims. Photograph the condition of the gear before you start as evidence, and if the wind and waves are unusually strong, push it to another day.

blocks.text: Beach Chairs, Umbrellas and Seaside Restaurants

blocks.html: Tawaen Beach has beach chairs and umbrellas to rent lined up along the whole shore, so you can sit and catch the breeze without laying out your own mat. Most charge per set per day, and some let you use them free if you order food or drinks from the restaurant that runs that zone. Before you sit, ask clearly how they charge so there's no confusion when the bill comes.

items: Beach chair + umbrella — rented as a daily set, roughly a few hundred THB per set; some places discount it or throw it in free if you order food and drinks. Ask the terms before you sit

Seaside restaurants — fresh seafood, stir-fried dishes, som tum, snacks and drinks. You can order it right to your chair. Prices on the island run a bit higher than on the Pattaya side because everything is hauled over by boat
Toilets and showers — available for a small per-use fee, so keep coins or small notes handy. Rinsing off before the ferry back makes the trip easier
Natural shade — there are trees along parts of the beach for shade, but in high season people grab those spots fast, so come early for a better position

blocks.text: A Day at Tawaen Beach — How to Plan Your Time

blocks.html: If you're doing Koh Larn as a day trip with Tawaen Beach as your base, here's a schedule built to dodge the crowds, so you get your swim, your water sports, and your lunch without rushing.

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.title: Catch the first ferry, claim a chair before the crowd

items.activity: Arrive at Bali Hai Pier, buy a ferry ticket or charter a speedboat
items.note: Go early to dodge the ferry queue and the traffic into Pattaya

items.activity: Ferry docks at Tawaen Beach, find a well-placed beach chair, ask the price before sitting
items.note: Arrive early and you get to pick a shaded zone

items.activity: Swim while the water's still clear, photograph the beach before it gets packed
items.note: Shallow water is fine to wade in; watch the warning flags for waves

items.activity: Try the water sports you want, banana boat, parasailing, or snorkeling
items.note: Ask the price clearly and check the life jacket before you start

items.activity: Seaside seafood lunch, order prawns, shellfish, fish, or stir-fried dishes
items.note: Ask the price per kilo and ask them to weigh it in front of you before ordering

items.activity: Lounge on the beach chair in the breeze, let the food settle before going back in
items.note: Let your stomach rest before swimming so you don't cramp

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.title: Catch some photos, rinse off, then head back

items.activity: Take a songthaew to Samae Beach or a viewpoint for photos, if you still have the energy
items.note: Allow time for travel on the island; ask the songthaew fare before getting on

items.activity: Head back to Tawaen Beach, rinse off in the showers, pack up
items.note: Keep coins or small notes for the toilet fee

items.activity: Catch the ferry back to Bali Hai, allow time for the queue when everyone heads back at once
items.note: Don't cut it close to the last ferry; it's better to leave a buffer

blocks.text: Things to Know Before You Go to Tawaen Beach

items: Weekends are crowded and ferries fill up — Saturdays, Sundays and long weekends overflow, with long ferry queues both ways. Going early and leaving before the late afternoon is far easier

Check the price and safety before any water sport — ask the price clearly, confirm per ride or per person, check the life jacket and the gear, and settle the damage terms, especially for jet skis, before you pay

The sea is murky on some days depending on the weather — how clear the water is depends on the weather and the wind and waves that day. Some days the water isn't as clear as in the photos, which is just nature. Check the forecast before you go
Bring cash — shops, beach chairs, songthaew fares and many water-sports operators mainly take cash. The signal and card machines on the island aren't always reliable
Help keep the beach clean — take your rubbish back or bin it properly, don't throw it in the sea, and help keep Tawaen Beach and Koh Larn clean and pretty for the long run
Pack enough sun protection — the island sun is strong, so use waterproof sunscreen, wear a hat and sunglasses, and keep drinking water

blocks.html: The short version: Tawaen Beach suits people who want it all in one beach, swimming, water sports, a chair to lounge in the breeze, and restaurants, traded against the noise and crowds on weekends. If you want a quieter beach, you can move on to Samae, Nuan or Thian as alternatives.

faq.q: How do you get to Tawaen Beach on Koh Larn, and where does the ferry land?
faq.a: Take the big passenger ferry from Bali Hai Pier in Pattaya, fare around 30 THB per trip, taking roughly 40–45 min. Many ferry runs dock directly at Tawaen Beach pier. If you want to go faster, charter a speedboat for about 15–20 min, paying roughly 150–200 THB per head on a shared boat, or a few thousand THB and up to charter the whole boat depending on size. Some big-ferry runs land at Na Ban pier instead, so check the sign before boarding.

faq.q: What water sports are at Tawaen Beach, and roughly how much do they cost?
faq.a: There's a full lineup: banana boat around 100–300 THB per person, parasailing around 500–800 THB per ride, jet ski around 800–1,200 THB per 30 min, while sea walker and snorkeling are often sold as packages. The prices are rough ranges that shift with the season and bargaining. Before any activity, ask the price clearly, check the life jacket and the gear, and always settle the damage terms before you pay.

faq.q: Does Tawaen Beach have beach chairs to rent, and how do they charge?
faq.a: Yes, beach chairs and umbrellas are lined up along the whole shore for rent. Most charge as a daily set in the few-hundred-THB range, and some discount it or let you sit free if you order food and drinks from the restaurant running that zone. Before you sit, ask the terms clearly so there's no confusion when the bill comes. It's crowded on weekends, so come early for a better spot and a shaded zone.

faq.q: What's the best day to go to Tawaen Beach to avoid the crowds?
faq.a: Weekdays are far less crowded than weekends, so if you can go on a weekday it's the most relaxed. But if you go on a Saturday, Sunday or long weekend, catch one of the first ferries in the morning so you get a well-placed beach chair, skip the water-sports queues, and enjoy clear water before the crowd wades in. On the way back, allow extra time for the ferry queue since people tend to head back together in the late afternoon.

faq.q: Is the water at Tawaen Beach always clear?
faq.a: How clear the water is depends on the weather and the wind and waves on any given day. On a calm, sunny day the water is clear and pretty, but on days with strong wind and waves or a lot of swimmers, it can be murkier than in the photos, which is just nature. Check the forecast before you go, and if you want clearer water, swim in the morning before the crowd arrives.
